problem: Given that $f(9.6)=3$ and $f(10.4)=11,$ find an approximation for ${f}^{′}(10).$

activity_context.topic_title: Estimating Derivatives Using a Central Difference Quotient

feedback.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{f}^{′}(x)≈\frac{f(x+h)-f(x-h)}{2h}
$$

 
at the point $x=5$ with the step size $h=0.1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ≈\frac{f(x+h)-f(x-h)}{2h} \\ {f}^{′}(5) & ≈\frac{f(5+0.1)-f(5-0.1)}{2(0.1)} \\  & =\frac{f(5.1)-f(4.9)}{0.2} \\  & =\frac{2.36-3.12}{0.2} \\  & =\frac{(-0.76)}{0.2} \\  & =-3.8.\end{aligned}
$$
